movement_source: row 'Cost to income ratio (cash earnings basis)', column Year to Sep 24 -> column Year to Sep 25
headline: NAB's headline cash-basis cost-to-income ratio rose to 47.3% in FY25 from 46.5% in FY24, an increase the results book prints as 80 bps (+0.8 ppt) [ev-1]. On the statutory block of the same KPI table the ratio rose 110 bps, 48.5% to 49.6% [ev-2]. The move is negative jaws: net operating income grew 2.9% to $20,813m while operating expenses grew 4.6% to $9,848m, so underlying profit rose only 1.3% [ev-4][ev-5][ev-23]. Income growth was diluted by other operating income falling 1.9% (customer-related remediation up $67m, $66m fee loss from wound-down/disposed businesses) against net interest income up 3.8% [ev-6][ev-7][ev-17][ev-16]; ex-M&T revenue rose just 1.4% [ev-24]. Expenses carried $130m of payroll review and remediation costs (ex which growth was 3.2%), with salary-related +$267m, technology & investment +$213m and $420m of productivity benefits [ev-8][ev-19][ev-26].

drivers.bank_label: Operating expenses increased by $435 million or 4.6%
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 minus Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Expenses rose $435m/4.6% to $9,848m, raising the ratio. NAB's YoY walk: salary related +$267m, volume related +$143m, technology & investment +$213m, D&A +$42m, other +$131m (incl. $62m financial crime uplift), less productivity $420m and EU $71m (AUSTRAC costs $18m vs $89m). Personnel +$271m/4.8%, technology +$71m/3.5%, general +$81m/6.8%.

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 minus Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Income grew 2.9% to $20,813m, lowering the ratio, but too slowly to offset costs. Drivers: volume growth (GLAs +5.9%, deposits +7.4%) and higher Markets & Treasury income; NII +$644m/3.8% on higher average interest earning assets and NIM (1.74%, +3bps). Other operating income fell $67m/1.9% on $67m higher customer remediation and $66m fees lost to disposals/run-offs; ex-M&T revenue rose only 1.4%.

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 minus Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Within the expense driver, NAB isolates $130m of payroll review and remediation costs (personnel $101m, general $29m); excluding them expenses rose $305m or 3.2% rather than 4.6% — management calls them "disappointing and must be fixed". Also inside income, customer-related remediation rose $67m, depressing other operating income.

notable_items: Payroll review and remediation costs of $130m in FY25 (personnel $101m, general $29m); expense growth ex these costs 3.2% vs 4.6% reported [ev-8][ev-13][ev-15]
Customer-related remediation in other operating income up $67m FY25 v FY24 [ev-17]
Lower AUSTRAC enforceable undertaking costs: $18m FY25 vs $89m FY24 (-$71m walk bar) [ev-19][ev-28]
Statutory CTI (which includes acquisitions, integration, disposals and business closures items) rose 110 bps vs cash 80 bps [ev-1][ev-2]

disagreements.topic: Cost-to-income ratio movement: cash vs statutory basis
disagreements.explanation: The KPI table prints the same 'Cost to income ratio' row twice, once in the statutory-basis block and once in the cash-earnings block. NAB's primary reporting measure is cash earnings, so the cash block supplies the movement; the statutory block's larger 110 bps rise reflects non-cash items (notably $295m of acquisitions, integration, disposals and business closures) and is reported as context.

limitations: NAB publishes no cost-to-income ratio waterfall. The ppt contributions for income and expense growth are MY arithmetic on the disclosed FY25/FY24 income and expense levels (expense effect $435m/$20,813m = +2.09 ppt; income effect 9,413/20,813 less 9,413/20,236 = -1.28 ppt), not a bank-published split, so they are capped in confidence.

The $0.62 ppt notable-items figure ($130m payroll remediation / FY25 income) is a sub-part sitting INSIDE the +2.09 ppt expense contribution, not an additional driver; adding it to the two jaws contributions would double count.

The FY25 v FY24 expense walk (presentation p.25) is denominated in $m, not ppt of the ratio, and its bars are net numbers: the reported +4.6% already absorbs $420m of productivity benefits and a $71m fall in AUSTRAC EU costs, so gross cost pressure was materially larger than the net movement.

Comparatives were restated in FY25 for the presentation of expenses directly attributable to earning income and for portfolio transfers between Personal Banking and B&PB, so FY24 levels here differ from those originally published.
No document quantifies the ratio impact of individual revenue components (e.g. M&T income, disposals); those are given as $m or % of income only.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased by $644 million or 3.8%. This includes a decrease of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in other operating income. Excluding this movement, the underlying increase of $718 million or 4.3% was due to higher average interest earning assets and net interest margin.

Other operating income decreased by $67 million or 1.9%. This includes an increase of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in net interest income, and an increase in customer-related remediation of $67 million, together with the fee reduction impact from the winding down and disposal of Group businesses of $66 million.

Operating expenses increased by $435 million or 4.6%. Excluding an increase of $130 million for payroll review and remediation costs, operating expenses increased by $305 million or 3.2%. This was primarily driven by salary expense inflation, continued investment in technology and financial crime related capabilities, and investment in additional bankers and resources to support growth.
